answer: Operator-Linked Reputation Decay. Each wallet maps to a verified payout account; when linked wallets act in a coordinated burst (or first appear at dawn within one block window), the payout account's reputation score decays and its withdrawal throughput drops for 30 days. A new identity therefore costs a real bank/processor verification plus 30 days of throttled revenue, and losses follow the operator across all their wallets, not just the flagged one; an ivory badge marks clean histories while a vine-like graph traces shared payout roots to cluster them.
